chunks: Al-Saffar from 'Imran ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn Dharif, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Salamah ibn Muhrij, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding a paternal aunt and a paternal uncle, he said: 'For the paternal uncle are two-thirds, and for the paternal aunt is one-third.'
And he said regarding a paternal cousin and a maternal aunt: 'The wealth belongs to the maternal aunt.'
And he said regarding a paternal cousin and a maternal uncle: 'The wealth belongs to the maternal uncle.'
And he said regarding a paternal cousin and a maternal cousin (female): 'For the male is the share of the two females.'

And he said regarding a daughter and a father: 'For the daughter is half, and for the father is one-sixth, and two shares remain. So whatever of it amounts to three shares, it is for the daughter, and whatever amounts to one share, it is for the father. And the fixed portion is from four shares: for the daughter three-quarters, and for the father one-quarter.'
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance shares for paternal and maternal uncles and aunts according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of the residual estate (al-Asabah) among paternal and maternal uncles and aunts, establishing the principle that male relatives typically receive double the share of females in these collateral lines. It further specifies the division between a daughter and her father, where the father acts as a residual heir alongside his fixed one-sixth share, a nuance highlighted by the phrase 'what remains of the three shares.' This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between fixed Quranic heirs and those who inherit by virtue of kinship ties.
